1: Chapter 1: The Customer on a Rainy Night
It had been raining for three days in Doldari Village. Kim Haneul's older sister had left for Seoul in the spring, and since then Haneul had been running the village's small pharmacy on her own.
At dusk, she shut the outer door, counted the day's earnings, put out the lantern, and went upstairs.
She had only just lain down when urgent knocking sounded at the door downstairs, followed by a man's voice. “Is anyone here?”

Outside the door stood a young man, soaked to the skin. The cloth wrapped around his left arm was stained with blood. He introduced himself as Park Junho and said he was from the Azure Dragon Society.
“Please treat my wounds,” Park Junho said in a low voice. “I'll pay you. Would three thousand five hundred nyang do?”
He took out a letter wrapped in oiled paper from his coat. “This letter must be delivered to Cheongpungsa by the eighteenth of the fifth month.”
Haneul thought to herself. Her neighbors had been complaining that the pharmacy was doing so well, and now a stranger had come calling in the middle of the night, too.
Even so, Haneul did not take the money and only said, “I'll guide you into the mountains early tomorrow morning.”
2: As soon as day broke, the two of them set out. Haneul had a basket strapped to her back, containing rice balls, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain, they met Lee Youngsoo, an old man chopping firewood. The old man set down his axe and spoke in a low voice. The previous evening, three strangers had come to the outskirts of the village looking for a young man who had been injured.
“Haneul, take the side path,” Lee Youngsoo said. “The main road is dangerous.” Haneul thanked the old man.
The side path was narrow and slippery. Haneul led the way, planting each foot firmly as she went. Park Junho followed behind her in silence.

At noon, the rain stopped, and as the mountain mist slowly lifted, the roof of Cheongpungsa began to come into view in the distance. A monk in a purple robe stood at the temple gate. It was Jeonghye, the monk who greeted guests at the temple.
Jeonghye accepted the letter, checked the red seal on its envelope, and nodded. “The abbot has been waiting for this letter for two years.”
Park Junho said to Haneul, “I owe you my life.” Haneul smiled and replied, “Then when you come next time, please fix the apothecary’s roof for me.” Park Junho stayed at the temple.
Toward evening, Haneul came down the mountain alone. By the time she reached home, it was already dark. She lit the oil lamp and sat for a long while behind the counter.
